reasons: Hugh claims a service-clock visit inside the alcove at 6:45, but the independently timed curtain was locked from 6:38 to 7:00.
Unlike other late visitors, he describes a brass corner post from the superseded cabinet design. The actual installation photographed at 6:31 is an open steel cradle with an external lamp.
Several early cabinet stories are also false, including my own; several late open-cradle stories have false timing. Hugh combines both kinds of falsehood and acknowledges earlier salon business.
His forged-sale liability supplies motive, though it would not identify him by itself.
confusion: As an innocent player, I am instructed to read a physical description that the photograph proves false. Why am I lying about that task? My private brief only describes buying back embarrassing paintings. I need a clear private explanation of my cover story so I do not inadvertently correct it aloud.
Alcove, gallery and balcony must be clearly distinguished in a diagram visible while questions are asked.
The repeated 'My other business that evening...' endings make people sound alike and draw attention to deliberate templating.
improvements: Give each innocent liar a specific private reason for the cover story and say to stick to the printed account until Coming Clean.
Use visibly different wording and cadence for the common cover-story explanations.

Keep the proposal and installation photographs available side by side during discussion, and provide a neutral chance to ask suspects to clarify their descriptions without coaching which facts matter.
Do not announce that the winning answer is whoever fails both checks; that would reduce the mystery to an intersection exercise.
accidental_reveal_risks: An innocent player who notices their own printed account is untrue may improvise a correction before Coming Clean.
The host could unintentionally coach the solution by emphasizing only timing and cabinet details.
A murderer could accidentally read the private confession or branch heading if page-stop instructions are not strong.
experience: The images make the investigation substantially more enjoyable than a purely verbal schedule puzzle. At first everybody has motive; after Act II several people still look suspicious; the final photographs let me narrow it. With a perfect transcript I can solve it, but listening to sixteen speeches at dinner would be appreciably harder. The printed lies need more roleplaying support.
limitations: Independent staged transcript assessment; no live table interruptions, memory loss, physical hunt or real-time discussion measured.
